description.content:
Creates a new quote in `Draft` status, owned by the user identified by the token sent with the request. The quote starts private and it is visible only to its creator until it is submitted for review.

Only the minimum item data is accepted in `negotiation.items` — the SKU, the seller, and the quantity. Catalog and pricing data is filled in automatically from a Checkout simulation, so prices returned in the response may differ from the store's list prices once contract or promotion rules apply.

To create a quote from a cart the shopper has already assembled, use the [Import cart as quote](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/quotes-api#post-/api/quoting/quotes/import) endpoint instead.

>⚠️ This feature is only available for stores using B2B Buyer Portal, which is currently available to select accounts.


## Permissions

This API does not rely on [License Manager resources](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/license-manager-resources--3q6ztrC8YynQf6rdc6euk3). Authorization is role based: the Quotes API derives the caller's role from the [user token](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/api-authentication-using-user-tokens) sent with the request, pairing the cookie the token travels in with the token's audience. A token with the store audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie_{accountName}` cookie resolves to the **Buyer** role, and a token with the VTEX Admin audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie` cookie resolves to the **Admin** role. A token sent in the other cookie is not accepted, and when both roles resolve in the same request, the Buyer role prevails.

A buyer may send the quote's `label` and most negotiation terms, including `items`, `serviceLocation`, `shipping`, `payment`, and `customData`. A buyer may never send `owner`, `ownerRole`, `participants`, `linkedContract`, `negotiation.customer`, `negotiation.shopper`, or `negotiation.items[].charge.value.adjustments`: any of these rejects the whole request with a `403` error whose `rejectedFields` array names the offending fields. An Admin may send every editable field, and must inform `negotiation.customer` explicitly, since an Admin token does not carry a customer.

Requests whose role cannot be determined are rejected with a `403` error.

(Required) HTTP Client Negotiation _Accept_ Header. Indicates the types of responses the client can understand.

Retrieves a paginated list of the quotes in the account, with optional filters and ordering. Filters on different fields are combined with a logical `AND`, while multiple values of the `status` filter are combined with a logical `OR`.

The response returns a compact projection of each quote. To read the full negotiation terms, use the [Get quote by ID](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/quotes-api#get-/api/quoting/quotes/-quoteId-) endpoint.

>❗ This endpoint is served by a search index that is eventually consistent. A quote created or updated moments earlier may not be reflected in the results yet.

>⚠️ This feature is only available for stores using B2B Buyer Portal, which is currently available to select accounts.


## Permissions

This API does not rely on [License Manager resources](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/license-manager-resources--3q6ztrC8YynQf6rdc6euk3). Authorization is role based: the Quotes API derives the caller's role from the [user token](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/api-authentication-using-user-tokens) sent with the request, pairing the cookie the token travels in with the token's audience. A token with the store audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie_{accountName}` cookie resolves to the **buyer** role, and a token with the VTEX Admin audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie` cookie resolves to the **Admin** role. A token sent in the other cookie is not accepted, and when both roles resolve in the same request, the buyer role prevails.

Any authenticated user of the account can list the account's quotes. There is no per-user filter on this endpoint: the results include every quote in the account, including quotes created by other users and quotes still in `Draft` status.

Requests whose role cannot be determined are rejected with a `403` error.

Creates a quote from a cart the shopper has already assembled, copying its items, delivery terms, and payment terms into the quote's negotiation. This is the entry point used by the checkout, where the shopper turns the cart they are looking at into a draft quote or into a quotation request in a single step.

The `label` is limited to 200 characters.

Set `submit` to `false` to keep the quote in `Draft`, so the requester can revise it before sending it. Set it to `true` to create and submit the quote atomically, leaving it in `Requested` status and visible to the counterpart.

>⚠️ This feature is only available for stores using B2B Buyer Portal, which is currently available to select accounts.


## Permissions

This API does not rely on [License Manager resources](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/license-manager-resources--3q6ztrC8YynQf6rdc6euk3). Authorization is role based: the Quotes API derives the caller's role from the [user token](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/api-authentication-using-user-tokens) sent with the request, pairing the cookie the token travels in with the token's audience. A token with the store audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie_{accountName}` cookie resolves to the **buyer** role, and a token with the VTEX Admin audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie` cookie resolves to the **Admin** role. A token sent in the other cookie is not accepted, and when both roles resolve in the same request, the buyer role prevails.

Both the buyer and the Admin roles can import a cart. The caller becomes the creator and the owner of the resulting quote.

Requests whose role cannot be determined are rejected with a `403` error.
(Required) Type of the content being sent.
(Required) HTTP Client Negotiation _Accept_ Header. Indicates the types of responses the client can understand.

Retrieves a single quote with its full negotiation terms, lifecycle timestamps, and any advisory warnings recorded by the last write operation.

Use the `status` and `expiresAt` fields to decide whether a quote can still be acted upon. A quote whose `expiresAt` has passed is moved to `Expired` by a background process, which is a terminal status.

>⚠️ This feature is only available for stores using B2B Buyer Portal, which is currently available to select accounts.


## Permissions

This API does not rely on [License Manager resources](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/license-manager-resources--3q6ztrC8YynQf6rdc6euk3). Authorization is role based: the Quotes API derives the caller's role from the [user token](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/api-authentication-using-user-tokens) sent with the request, pairing the cookie the token travels in with the token's audience. A token with the store audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie_{accountName}` cookie resolves to the **buyer** role, and a token with the VTEX Admin audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie` cookie resolves to the **Admin** role. A token sent in the other cookie is not accepted, and when both roles resolve in the same request, the buyer role prevails.

Any authenticated user of the account can read a quote, including quotes created by other users and quotes in `Draft` status. While a quote is in `InReview` status, reading it requires the Admin role — any admin can read it, not only the reviewer named in `assignedReviewerId`.

Requests whose role cannot be determined are rejected with a `403` error.
(Required) Unique identifier of the quote.
(Required) HTTP Client Negotiation _Accept_ Header. Indicates the types of responses the client can understand.

Changes the content of a quote that is in `Draft` or `InReview` status. Only the fields sent in the payload are evaluated, and the request is atomic: if any part of it is rejected, nothing is persisted.

Changes applied while the quote is in `Draft` or `InReview` status do not seal a version. In every other status the quote is not editable, and this endpoint returns a `422` error.

To change item quantities, send the item `id` along with the new `quantity`. To add an item, send its `id`, `seller`, and `quantity`. Omitting an item that is currently in the quote removes it.

>⚠️ This feature is only available for stores using B2B Buyer Portal, which is currently available to select accounts.


## Permissions

This API does not rely on [License Manager resources](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/license-manager-resources--3q6ztrC8YynQf6rdc6euk3). Authorization is role based: the Quotes API derives the caller's role from the [user token](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/api-authentication-using-user-tokens) sent with the request, pairing the cookie the token travels in with the token's audience. A token with the store audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie_{accountName}` cookie resolves to the **buyer** role, and a token with the VTEX Admin audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie` cookie resolves to the **Admin** role. A token sent in the other cookie is not accepted, and when both roles resolve in the same request, the buyer role prevails.

Only the user who created the quote can change it while it is in `Draft` status, and only the assigned reviewer can change it while it is in `InReview` status. A buyer may change the quote's `label` and most negotiation terms, including `items`, `serviceLocation`, `shipping`, `payment`, and `customData`. A buyer may never send `owner`, `ownerRole`, `participants`, `linkedContract`, `negotiation.customer`, `negotiation.shopper`, or `negotiation.items[].charge.value.adjustments`. On items already in the quote, a buyer may only change `quantity`: sending `productId`, `name`, `seller`, `charge`, `parentItemIds`, or `options` is rejected. Any rejected field fails the whole request with a `403` error whose `rejectedFields` array names the offending fields. An Admin may change every editable field.

While the quote is in `InReview` status, `negotiation.customer` and `negotiation.shopper` are read-only for every role, and sending either returns a `403 DRAFT_EDIT_FORBIDDEN` error with the `inreview_identity_readonly` reason.

Requests whose role cannot be determined are rejected with a `403` error.

The quote must have at least one item to be submitted.

Completes the review and sends the quote back to the requesting party, moving it from `InReview` to `Reviewed`. This action seals a new version of the quote, preserving the terms as they stand at this moment.

From `Reviewed`, the requesting party can convert the quote into a cart, decline it, or retract it to `Draft` to start another negotiation round. Completing the review also records an implicit approval for the reviewer.

>⚠️ This feature is only available for stores using B2B Buyer Portal, which is currently available to select accounts.

Converts an agreed quote into a cart, moving it to `ConvertedToCart` and returning the `orderFormId` of the new cart. The negotiated terms are carried over to the cart. Before returning, the service stamps the quote's identifier onto the cart under the `quotes` custom data app, in the `quoteId` field, sets the cart to expire at the same moment as the quote, and then locks the cart so the shopper cannot change the negotiated terms before placing the order.

The quote's `cartId` field is filled with the same identifier.

A quote can be converted from any status except `Declined`, `Expired`, and `ConvertedToCart`, which all return a `422 QUOTE_ALREADY_CONVERTED` error. The quote must also carry both `negotiation.shipping` and `negotiation.payment`, otherwise conversion fails with a `QUOTE_CONVERSION_INVALID_DATA` error.

>❗ A quote can only be converted once.

>⚠️ This feature is only available for stores using B2B Buyer Portal, which is currently available to select accounts.

Retrieves the audit trail of a quote, oldest version first. The first page starts at version `1` and `versionNumber` increases down the list. A version is sealed every time the quote changes outside the `Draft` and `InReview` statuses, which means each submit and each completed review adds one entry.

Entries carry only the version header. To read the negotiation terms as they stood in a given version, use the [Get quote version](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/quotes-api#get-/api/quoting/quotes/-quoteId-/versions/-versionId-) endpoint.

Results are paginated with a cursor: when `nextCursor` is returned, send it back in the `cursor` parameter to fetch the next page. The absence of `nextCursor` means the last page was reached.

>⚠️ This feature is only available for stores using B2B Buyer Portal, which is currently available to select accounts.

## Permissions

This API does not rely on [License Manager resources](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/license-manager-resources--3q6ztrC8YynQf6rdc6euk3). Authorization is role based: the Quotes API derives the caller's role from the [user token](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/api-authentication-using-user-tokens) sent with the request, pairing the cookie the token travels in with the token's audience. A token with the store audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie_{accountName}` cookie resolves to the **buyer** role, and a token with the VTEX Admin audience sent in the `VtexIdclientAutCookie` cookie resolves to the **Admin** role. A token sent in the other cookie is not accepted, and when both roles resolve in the same request, the buyer role prevails.

Only the author of the comment can delete it.

Requests whose role cannot be determined are rejected with a `403` error.

description.content:
>⚠️ This feature is only available for stores using B2B Buyer Portal, which is currently available to select accounts.


The Quotes API manages commercial quotations, also known as requests for quotation (RFQ), between a store and its buyers. It supports the negotiation phase that precedes an order in B2B commerce: a buyer or a sales representative assembles a set of commercial terms, the counterpart reviews and revises them, and once both parties agree, the quote is converted into a [cart](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/checkout-api) that can be checked out as a regular order.

A quote holds the same commercial terms as a cart — items, quantities, prices, discounts, delivery method, and payment method — but has its own lifecycle, version history, and permission rules. The Quotes API does not replace the [Checkout API](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/checkout-api): it delegates pricing simulation and order placement to Checkout, and it does not run the full set of transactional validations that Checkout applies at order placement time.

## Quote lifecycle

Every quote moves through a state machine. The `status` field reflects the current stage, and each transition is triggered by a dedicated action endpoint.

| **Status** | **Description** |
| - | - |
| `Draft` | The quote was created but not yet submitted. Only its creator can change or submit it, but any authenticated user of the account can read it and see it in the quote list. Edits in this status do not create a version. |
| `Requested` | The quote was submitted and is pending review by the counterpart. |
| `InReview` | An admin acknowledged the quote and is working on it. Any admin can read it, but only the assigned reviewer can change it or complete the review. Edits in this status do not create a version. |
| `Reviewed` | The review is complete and the quote is back with the requesting party, who can approve it, convert it, decline it, or retract it to `Draft` to start a new round. |
| `Declined` | One of the parties declined the quote. This is a terminal status. |
| `Expired` | The `expiresAt` deadline passed. A background process applies this transition, and it is a terminal status. |
| `ConvertedToCart` | A cart was created from the quote. The `cartId` field holds the resulting `orderFormId`. |

Every change made to a quote outside the `Draft` and `InReview` statuses seals a new version, which keeps a full audit trail of the negotiation. Versions are available through the quote versions endpoints.

While a quote is in `Draft` status, only the user who created it can change it. A buyer may change the quote's `label` and most of its negotiation terms, including items, `serviceLocation`, `shipping`, `payment`, and `customData`. The fields a buyer can never send are `owner`, `ownerRole`, `participants`, `linkedContract`, `negotiation.customer`, `negotiation.shopper`, and `negotiation.items[].charge.value.adjustments`. On items that are already in the quote, a buyer may only change `quantity`: sending `productId`, `name`, `seller`, `charge`, `parentItemIds`, or `options` is rejected. Any rejected field causes the whole request to fail with a `403` error whose `rejectedFields` array names the offending fields. Admins may change any editable field of the drafts they created.

## Error codes

Errors share a common payload with a machine-readable `code`, a `message`, and a `retry` flag that tells whether the same request can be sent again unchanged.

| **Code** | **HTTP status** | **Description** |
| - | - | - |
| `MISSING_ACCOUNT_NAME` | 400 | The account could not be resolved from the request. |
| `MISSING_ITEMS_FIELD` | 400 | The `negotiation.items` field is missing from the payload. |
| `INVALID_SEARCH_QUERY` | 400 | One or more query parameters are invalid. The `details` field names each rejected parameter. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_IMPORT_SOURCE` | 400 | The `source` field holds a value other than `orderForm`. |
| `ORDERFORM_NOT_FOUND` | 400 | The cart informed in the `content` field does not exist. |
| `INCOMPLETE_ORDERFORM` | 400 | The cart informed in the `content` field lacks data required to build a quote. |
| `DECLINE_REASON_REQUIRED` | 400 | The `reason` field is missing or empty. |
| `COMMENT_CONTENT_INVALID` | 400 | The comment content is empty or exceeds 4,000 characters. |
| `INVALID_COMMENT_CURSOR` | 400 | The `cursor` query parameter is malformed or expired. |
| `INVALID_COMMENT_PAGE_SIZE` | 400 | The `pageSize` query parameter is outside the allowed range. |
| `DRAFT_EDIT_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | The caller is not the creator of the draft, their role could not be determined, or they tried to change the customer or shopper of a quote in `InReview` status. |
| `BUYER_WHITELIST_VIOLATION` | 403 | A buyer sent fields they are not allowed to change. The `rejectedFields` array names them. |
| `INREVIEW_ACCESS_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | The quote is in `InReview` status and the caller is not the assigned reviewer. |
| `RETRACT_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | The caller is not allowed to retract the quote to the requested status. |
| `DECLINE_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | The caller is not allowed to decline the quote. |
| `COMMENT_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | The caller is not allowed to read, write, or delete the comment. |
| `COMMENT_VISIBILITY_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Only Admins can create comments with `Internal` visibility. |
| `QUOTE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No quote with the given ID exists in the account. |
| `QUOTE_VERSION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The quote exists, but it has no version with the given ID. |
| `COMMENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The quote exists, but it has no comment with the given ID. |
| `QUOTE_NOT_COMMENTABLE` | 409 | The quote is in a status that does not accept comments. |
| `QUOTE_NOT_EDITABLE` | 422 | The quote is in a status that does not allow the requested change. |
| `QUOTE_NOT_SUBMITTABLE` | 422 | The quote is not in `Draft` status and cannot be submitted. |
| `SUBMIT_FORBIDDEN` | 422 | The caller is not the creator of the quote and cannot submit it. |
| `ACKNOWLEDGE_FORBIDDEN` | 422 | The caller is not the reviewer assigned to the quote. |
| `QUOTE_ITEMS_REQUIRED` | 422 | The quote has no items and the requested action requires at least one. |
| `QUOTE_ALREADY_CONVERTED` | 422 | The quote is in a status that cannot be converted: `ConvertedToCart`, `Declined`, or `Expired`. |
| `QUOTE_CONVERSION_INVALID_DATA` | 422 | The negotiation terms are not sufficient to build a cart. |
| `INVALID_PAYMENT_TOTAL` | 422 | The sum of the payment methods does not match the quote total. |
| `CHECKOUT_UNAVAILABLE` | 502 | The Checkout API did not respond. The request can be retried. |
| `SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | The search backend that serves the listing endpoint is unavailable. The request can be retried. |
| `QUOTE_STORE_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | The quote record store is unavailable. The request can be retried. |

Fields with no value are omitted from responses rather than returned as `null`.
